haiku-low.q1: The API reads reports.row_count from the replica. At 10,000 or fewer rows, it returns the CSV in the response (200) and the page saves it. Above 10,000, a background job builds it and the user gets an emailed link.
haiku-low.q2: A partial unique index on (user, report) for queued or running blocks the second insert, and the API returns the existing export instead of creating a new one.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 86,400 seconds (24 hours) after sending. The bucket deletes each file 7 days after creation. Stray uploads from failed attempts are discarded after 24 hours.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, with waits of 60 and 300 seconds. After the third failure, the handler sets status failed with the error text and emails the user. The page shows Failed with the error text.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows are read only from the read replica. The export status row is kept on the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: The status is stored in the report_exports row on the primary database. On load, the page calls the latest-export endpoint, so reopening shows the current status. While queued or running, it polls the export endpoint.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 500-row batches by row_id, never OFFSET, and sends a 5 MB multipart part each time the buffer fills. Only one batch and one part are in memory, so the largest report needs about 180 parts.
haiku-low.q8: On error the upload is aborted. On timeout or dead worker, the abort cannot run, so the stray upload stays invisible and is discarded after 24 hours. The next attempt restarts from the first row with the same export id, writing its own attempt-n.csv file.
haiku-low.q9: The filters and columns are stored in the report_exports row on the primary database. The job payload carries only export_id, so the job reads the filters and columns from that row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user, report) for queued or running statuses blocks the second insert at the database level.
haiku-low.q11: Before sending the email, the file must be completed and visible, and a signed link created. If the queue reruns a finished or done export, the job stops because status is done or failed.
haiku-low.q12: The download is incomplete. Nothing is stored, so the user has to click Download CSV again. The document does not say more about the partial response.

sonnet.q1: Step 1 reads reports.row_count from the replica. 10,000 or fewer: small path, the CSV is returned in the click's response (status 200) and the page saves it as a file. Above 10,000: background job; the API returns 202 with export id and status, the file is written to the exports bucket, and the user gets an email with a signed link valid 24 hours.
sonnet.q2: A partial unique index on (user, report) for statuses queued/running blocks a second insert. The API then returns the existing export instead of creating a new one (and if it is still queued, re-enqueues the job). Filters of the second request are ignored; the running export is returned.
sonnet.q3: The link works 24 hours (86,400 seconds). The bucket deletes each file 7 days after it was created (lifecycle rule, not a job).
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (retries after 60 s, then 300 s). After the third failure the queue calls the failure handler once, which sets status failed with the error text and emails the user that the export failed. The page then shows 'Failed: ' plus the error text, and Download CSV starts a new export.
sonnet.q5: The read replica for report rows (both small path and job). The export row itself/status is on the primary database.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports row on the primary database (status, owner, object_key, finished_at). The page polls GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/{export_id} while queued/running, status read from the primary. On reopening, it calls GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/latest on load and polls if the latest is queued or running. Nothing is kept in the browser.
sonnet.q7: By streaming: a multipart upload to exports/{export_id}/attempt-{n}.csv; reads rows from the replica in batches of 500 by row_id (no OFFSET); sends a part each time the buffer reaches 5 MB (about 180 parts at largest). Only one batch and one part are held in memory. Speed within the 30-minute limit is not measured (needs about 1,100 rows/s).
sonnet.q8: Nothing is kept between attempts and the next attempt restarts from the beginning (step 4, full export, no progress saved). On error the upload is aborted; if timeout or dead worker, the abort can't run, but the partial upload stays invisible and the bucket lifecycle rule discards it after 24 hours. The next attempt writes its own new file attempt-{n}.csv, never replacing an earlier file.
sonnet.q9: They are stored in the report_exports row on the primary database (with user and report), inserted at click time from the URL's filters and columns. The job payload carries only {export_id}, and the job loads the row to get them.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on (user, report) for statuses queued or running in the database; the second insert hits the index and the API returns the existing export.
sonnet.q11: Before the email: the upload must be completed (file visible at its key) and the signed link created; the email is sent before status is set to done. If the job runs again: step 4 loads the row and stops if status is done or failed. If the file is finished but status not yet done (e.g. lost write), the retry redoes the whole export with a new attempt file and may send the email twice. A different job that doesn't own it stops at the claim.
sonnet.q12: The download is incomplete; nothing is stored, and the user clicks Download CSV again.
